parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal document/facility rules plus state facility and trespass rules form one system the traveller passes through. Universal exposures dominate: passport markers locked to assigned sex with reported confiscation/stranding and visa-refusal cables; federal ban on identity-congruent facilities in government buildings; state bathroom bans (schools, colleges, 2026 expansion) with criminal trespass in some units and a documented arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward. No execution or likely imprisonment for visitors. Mitigation is real but partial: functioning courts, an injunction, legal-aid guidance, national hate-crime and employment rulings — yet litigation is unresolved and 66% back sex-at-birth document rules.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 bar on X markers and self-selection; markers fixed to assigned sex; travellers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; Feb 2025 cable orders refusal where sex is in doubt and considers fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; eight foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; ACLU suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can cascade into secondary screening, refusal, or fraud allegations feeding detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman under a state bathroom law (trespass, up to 60 days) with 24 hours held in the men's ward; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans detainees; corrections bureau applies conversion-therapy-style policies and stopped counting trans prisoners.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave; national courts denied a state's stay request and litigation continues; legal-aid FAQ exists.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A state facility stop can escalate into custody where federal/state custody practices then apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; 21+ units restrict facilities, 4 criminalise in circumstances, 6 reach private settings; this unit expanded its ban to colleges May 2026.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban; one plaintiff's equal-protection challenge is succeeding on injunction; exemptions cover assistance, emergencies, out-of-order facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules and state statutes overlap in public buildings a visitor may enter.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders defund and stigmatise gender-affirming care; subpoenas of under-19 patient records; state freeze-frame policy restricts trans inmates' treatment (resident/custody-facing).
care_services.protection: Emergency care for visitors not documented as denied; national employment and hate-crime statutes remain in force.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can expose identity through records; relevant mainly if detained or hospitalised.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame transition as 'mutilation' and direct investigations of 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; 66% poll supports sex-at-birth document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never include the phrase; strategy states CT powers won't target mere disagreement; same-sex marriage and employment protections intact.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that stops and screening become hostile.

minors_guardians.exposure: Criminal-referral order against teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; school/college bathroom bans bind any accompanying minor; youth crisis-lifeline services shut.
minors_guardians.protection: Litigation pending; some units lack bans; parental travel documents govern the child.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces the same document and facility regime plus school-linked exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime statute (confirmed 2007); only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes; 2025 arrest involved police acting on the facility ban; documented police/ICE abuse of trans detainees.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national bias statistics track orientation not identity; safety varies by unit with some protective scorecards.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak state recourse means street or custody violence against an outed visitor may go unremedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple orders blocked yet others in force; outcome depends on travel date; state-level patchwork; four units 'Do Not Travel'; no state hate-crime law; sodomy law unrepealed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning federal courts granting injunctions; ACLU litigation; legal-aid FAQ; equality maps track exposure; national employment and marriage protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial remedies reduce severity but universal document and facility exposures persist regardless.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register excludes trans visitors with no remedy. Here the federal document regime likewise produces exclusion/stranding with no real-time appeal, so documents sit near that anchor; but it is one dimension within a rule-of-law state where courts grant injunctions and litigation is live, so overall higher.

Closest match: routine exposure at checkpoints and services, documented detention/humiliation, prosecutions uncommon, remedies slow and inconsistent, uncertainty about which measures are operative on a given date. This dossier adds criminal trespass and custody-by-birth-sex risk, holding it at rather than above 0.45.

Kestrel Isles offers secondary screening and discretionary refusal but purely administrative outcomes. This jurisdiction is worse: criminal facility exposure, a documented arrest with men's-ward custody, and official hostile framing — hence below 0.55 despite comparable document friction.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one combined system: federal document rules fix markers to assigned sex (with reported confiscation and stranding) and bar identity-congruent facilities in federally funded buildings, while the division's 2024 ban, expanded to universities in May 2026, plus criminal trespass provisions in some units, govern public buildings. Universal exposures (documents, facilities) are continuous and state-imposed; the worst documented custody outcome — a trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom arrest — is severe but bounded (misdemeanour, no execution, imprisonment not typical). Functioning courts, an operative injunction, legal-aid guidance and national hate-crime/employment law partially offset, but litigation is unresolved, four units are 'Do Not Travel,' and public opinion backs the document regime — placing the case in Elevated Risk, above 0.35 anchors, below the 0.55 administrative-only anchors.
